title: A save system
description:
Save and load a game's state as Lua text, with versions and safety checks.

```
saved slot 1 (v3): 1.2 KB
loaded slot 1: level 4, 3 items, position (12, 7)
loading an old v1 save: upgraded to v3 (added "stamina")
broken file: refused (syntax error near line 4)
```

starter.main.lua:
local state = { version = 3, level = 4, items = { "map", "sword", "potion" }, pos = { x = 12, y = 7 } }
print(state.level, #state.items)

hints: Keep a list of upgrade functions, `upgrades[1]` turning v1 into v2 and so on, and apply them in a loop (lesson 8.03).
Sorting keys makes two saves of the same state identical, which makes problems easy to compare.
requirements: `save(state)` writes sorted, indented Lua source with a `version` field; `load_save(text)` reads it in an empty environment.
Upgrade functions turn version 1 and 2 saves into version 3.
Refuse functions, cycles and files that are not tables, with clear messages.
stretch: Add a checksum line so a hand-edited save is noticed.
